concerns.advisory: Both new gems are added to `Gemfile`, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is regenerated — the primary `Gemfile.lock` is untouched, so a deploy using the default lockfile will fail bundler's frozen check or resolve differently.
concerns.why: Gemfile adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss`; the diff only updates Gemfile_rails4.lock (guess_html_encoding, ruby-readability 0.5.7, simple-rss 1.3.1).

concerns.advisory: New assets `embed.js` and `embed.css.scss` are introduced and referenced by `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, but no asset precompile configuration is added, so in production the embed layout will 404 on its stylesheet unless the precompile list already covers these names.
concerns.why: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js and app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss are new top-level assets; app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`; no config/application.rb precompile change in the diff.

concerns.advisory: The already-committed migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` is edited in place to add `force: true`, which means installs that already ran it are unaffected but any re-run (or a rollback/replay, or a fresh dev DB rebuilt from a schema that has data) will silently DROP and recreate `top_topics`.
concerns.why: `create_table :top_topics` → `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in an existing dated migration; the new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`.

concerns.advisory: Imported feed/article HTML is stored with `cook_method = :raw_html` and rendered via `raw post.cooked`, bypassing Discourse's sanitizing cook pipeline entirely, so the security posture of embedded topics now depends wholly on ruby-readability's tag/attribute whitelist and the trustworthiness of the polled feed.
concerns.why: `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`; `TopicEmbed.import` passes that cook_method; `best.html.erb` emits `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. `import_remote` whitelists tags but `PollFeed` passes feed `content` straight through with no whitelist at all.

concerns.advisory: Both remote-fetch paths use Kernel#open (open-uri) on a URL, which fetches arbitrary internal/external hosts from the app server and — for open-uri — treats a leading `|` as a shell command; the only guard is an exact `embeddable_host` match in TopicRetriever, which `PollFeed`/`import_remote` do not themselves enforce.
concerns.why: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in poll_feed and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`; `import_remote` is also called directly from lib/tasks/disqus.thor with arbitrary thread links.

concerns.advisory: Any anonymous visitor hitting `embed/best` with an unknown embed_url enqueues a background job that performs an outbound HTTP fetch; the only rate limiting is a 60-second Redis key per exact URL, so distinct URL variants (query strings, fragments) each get their own fetch slot.
concerns.why: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` with no auth requirement, and `retrieved_recently?` keys on `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` for 60s.

concerns.advisory: Framing protection is deliberately disabled (`X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`) and replaced by a `request.referer` host comparison, which is client-supplied and omitted/spoofable, so the embed endpoint's access control is only as strong as the Referer header.

The postMessage handshake validates loosely on both ends: the child posts to `'<%= request.referer %>'` (a full URL, not an origin) and the parent accepts any message whose origin appears as a substring of `discourseUrl`, so origin checking is weaker than an equality comparison.
concerns.why: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` in layouts/embed.html.erb and `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in embed.js.

concerns.advisory: `PostRevisor#update_post` now honors a new `skip_validations` option that changes `@post.save` to `save(validate: false)` for every caller, widening a model-level invariant escape hatch beyond the embed import path that motivated it.
concerns.why: lib/post_revisor.rb: `@post.save` → `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`; only TopicEmbed.import passes the flag today.

concerns.advisory: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, so a single embed miss synchronously downloads and imports the entire configured feed (creating/revising many topics) inside one Sidekiq job before falling back to the single-URL fetch.
concerns.why: `if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?; Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}); ...` inside perform_retrieve, invoked from Jobs::RetrieveTopic.

concerns.advisory: The feed poller has no error handling and `retry: false`, so a single malformed feed, network timeout, or nil `i.content` silently loses that hourly run with nothing logged beyond the Sidekiq failure.
concerns.why: `sidekiq_options retry: false` plus unguarded `open(...)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, and `i.content.scrub` in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed.

concerns.advisory: `PollFeed#feed_key` computes a `feed-modified:` cache key that is never read or written anywhere, so the conditional-GET/change-detection it implies does not exist and every hourly poll refetches and re-hashes the whole feed.
concerns.why: `def feed_key; @feed_key ||= "feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}"; end` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, with no call sites in the diff.

concerns.advisory: `embed_url` is a plain `t.string` (255 chars on most adapters) carrying a unique index, so long article/feed URLs can be truncated or rejected and two long URLs sharing a prefix could collide on the unique index.

The loading page self-reloads every 30 seconds while the retrieval throttle is 60 seconds, so a visitor whose fetch is slow will reload into a throttled no-op at least once, and there is no give-up condition — the page reloads forever if retrieval never succeeds.
concerns.why: `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000)` in embed/loading.html.erb versus `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` in TopicRetriever.

concerns.advisory: The disqus thor task drops its `--category` option and switches topic creation to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, silently changing the importer's behavior (no category placement, one live HTTP fetch per thread, content now scraped from the link instead of a permalink stub) for anyone relying on the old flow.
concerns.why: lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes `method_option :category` and the `category_id` lookup, replacing `PostCreator.new(...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`.

concerns.advisory: Test coverage stops at the seams: `PollFeed#poll_feed`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and `absolutize_urls` edge cases (non-default ports, protocol-relative `//host/x`, relative paths without a leading slash) are never exercised, and the EmbedController specs stub out TopicView/TopicRetriever so the new views and layout are never rendered.
concerns.why: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only asserts the `execute` guard delegation; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb covers only `.import` with one root-relative URL; spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb mocks `TopicView.new` and the retriever.

concerns.advisory: The four new site settings are added with no type/format validation or client exposure, so `embeddable_host` accepts any string (scheme, port, or path included) even though it is compared against `URI(...).host`, and only a single embedding host is supportable.
concerns.why: config/site_settings.yml adds bare-string `embeddable_host`/`feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` defaults, while both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compare it to a parsed `.host`.
